newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - NZRFU to price rugby players.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - NZRFU to price rugby players.

text.p: Wellington, Sept 9 - Leading rugby players will have a price on their heads after the end of this year's National Provincial Championship, NZPA reports.
The New Zealand Rugby Football Union is moving this week to allow controlled trading of top rugby players between provinces.
The NZRFU's board will spend much of Wednesday going through a transfer fee paper prepared by union staff which will see players put on different levels depending on their skills and achievements.
NZRFU chief executive David Moffett would not comment on the paper's content, but said it was expected to generate vigorous debate.
"We have to get our house in order before the end of the season and the transfer system will be in operation by November," Moffett said.

It is believed the system, which will replace the one-year moratorium on players shifting provinces, will place All Blacks, Super 12 players and NPC players on different fee levels, with their new unions having to pay considerable money to the unions from which they transfer.
To assist in rating players, unions are expected to be asked to name their top 15 players. Potential All Blacks not included in these groups will also be rated for transfer.

It's expected the fees will also be applied to age-groups, such as New Zealand Colts and under-19, to prevent wholesale "buying" of young players without recompense to unions which develop them. The aim is to ensure all top players get regular good-level match play.

The NZRFU board has other important business this week -- tomorrow will be spent on the union's strategic plan as developed by Moffett and his staff, while Waikato and North Harbour have the chance to make written and oral submissions on Wednesday on whether the Waikato Chiefs base should remain at Hamilton or shift to the new North Harbour Albany stadium.

The board will also decide how many tests will be played by the All Blacks in the southern hemisphere next year, with Moffett saying test dates for the tour of England and Wales late in the year were still open to negotiation.
The board will also receive recommendations for Super 12 coaches.

* South Africa is expected to adopt the regional concept used in New Zealand for next year's Super 12 competition. The South African Rugby Football Union is tomorrow expected to okay proposals to have the following groupings:
Western Province, Eastern Province and small neighbours; Natal and Orange Free State; Transvaal and Griqualand West; Northern Transvaal and small neighbours.
